issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch for the farm song: the problem statement (and the template Farm.java) define/expect a public method singFarmSong() to play the song, but the solution implements a public method named playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). Additionally, the solution's Main.java (and the template Main.java) still reference farm.singFarmSong(), but solution's Farm.java does not provide that method. This inconsistency will prevent students/tests from finding the expected singFarmSong() API and may cause compilation or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public API consistent: rename the solution's playFarmSong() method to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to playFarmSong(). Also update any Main.java references to call the chosen method name so that the template, problem statement, tests, and solution all use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and template specify a public method named singFarmSong() in Farm to play the song, but the solution implementation names this method playFarmSong(). This is the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students when mapping requirements (and template stubs) to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() so that the method identifier matches the problem statement and the template stub (or alternatively, change the problem/template to use playFarmSong()). Aligning to singFarmSong() preserves the original task wording and reduces cognitive mapping load.
